indicator.objective: Identify causes, symptoms and prevention of measles

skills.description: Recognise that measles is caused by a germ that spreads from person to person.
Identify common symptoms of measles (e.g. fever, rash, cough, red eyes).
Describe simple ways measles spreads (e.g. coughing, sneezing, close contact).
Identify ways to prevent measles (e.g. vaccination, keeping away from infected persons, covering mouth when coughing).
State what to do if someone is exposed to or shows signs of measles (tell an adult, see a health worker).
Organise causes, symptoms and prevention of measles in a simple concept map or poster.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Measles is caused by dirty water.
Measles cannot spread from one person to another.
A rash is the only sign of measles.
Measles is the same as malaria.
You should hide a sick person from health workers.

questions.stem: What causes measles?
options: A germ that spreads from person to person
hints: Measles spreads between people.
It is caused by a tiny germ.
questions.explanation: Measles is caused by a germ that spreads from one person to another.
questions.misconception: Measles is caused by dirty water.

questions.stem: Which of these is a common symptom of measles?
hints: Measles affects the skin.
A rash is a common sign.
questions.explanation: A rash on the skin is a common symptom of measles.
questions.misconception: A rash is the only sign of measles.

questions.stem: How can measles spread from one person to another?
hints: Think about droplets from the mouth and nose.
Coughing and sneezing send germs into the air.
questions.explanation: Measles can spread through coughing and sneezing, which send germs into the air.
questions.misconception: Measles cannot spread from one person to another.

questions.stem: Which of these helps prevent measles?
hints: A vaccine protects you from diseases.
Measles can be prevented by vaccination.
questions.explanation: Vaccination helps prevent measles by protecting the body against the germ.
questions.misconception: Vaccination does not prevent measles.

questions.stem: What should you do if you think someone has measles?
options: Tell an adult and see a health worker
hints: A health worker can help.
Tell an adult you trust.
questions.explanation: If someone shows signs of measles, tell an adult and see a health worker for help.
questions.misconception: You should hide a sick person from health workers.

questions.stem: Ama says, 'Measles is caused by dirty water.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, measles comes from dirty water
No, measles is caused by a germ that spreads from person to person
No, measles is caused by too much sun
No, measles is caused by eating too much
hints: Measles spreads between people.
It is not caused by water.
questions.explanation: Measles is caused by a germ that spreads from person to person, not by dirty water.
questions.misconception: Measles is caused by dirty water.

questions.stem: Which set lists common symptoms of measles?
hints: Measles causes fever and rash.
A cough is also common.
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of measles include fever, rash and cough. Red eyes may also occur.
questions.misconception: A rash is the only sign of measles.

questions.stem: Why should a person with measles cover their mouth when coughing?
options: To stop germs from spreading to others
hints: Coughing sends germs into the air.
Covering the mouth traps the germs.
questions.explanation: Covering the mouth when coughing helps stop the measles germs from spreading to other people.
questions.misconception: Measles cannot spread from one person to another.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way to prevent measles from spreading in a school?
options: Keeping a sick learner away from others
hints: Sick learners should rest at home.
Keeping away reduces spread.
questions.explanation: Keeping a sick learner away from others helps prevent measles from spreading in the school.
questions.misconception: Measles cannot spread in school.

questions.stem: Kofi sits near a learner who has measles. What should Kofi do?
options: Tell the teacher and wash his hands
hints: Tell an adult.
Wash hands to stay clean.
questions.explanation: Kofi should tell the teacher and wash his hands. The teacher can then take the right steps to protect others.
questions.misconception: You should hide a sick person.

questions.stem: Name two symptoms of measles.
hints: Measles causes a skin rash.
Fever is also common.
questions.explanation: Common symptoms of measles include fever, rash, cough and red eyes.
questions.misconception: A rash is the only sign of measles.

questions.stem: Give one way to prevent measles.
hints: A vaccine protects you.
Avoid close contact with sick people.
questions.explanation: Measles can be prevented by vaccination, avoiding close contact with infected persons, and covering the mouth when coughing.
questions.misconception: Vaccination does not prevent measles.

questions.stem: Draw a simple concept map showing the causes, symptoms and prevention of measles. Use three groups: 'Causes', 'Symptoms' and 'Prevention'. Write at least two points under each group.

criteria.description: Wrote at least two correct causes of measles
Wrote at least two correct symptoms of measles
Wrote at least two correct ways to prevent measles
Organised the points clearly under the three headings

hints: Think about the germ that causes measles.
Think about fever and rash.
Think about vaccination and covering the mouth.
questions.explanation: This is a written task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Measles cannot be prevented.

questions.stem: What causes measles?
answer: a germ that spreads from person to person
measles is caused by a germ
hints: It is a tiny living thing.
It spreads between people.
questions.explanation: Measles is caused by a germ that spreads from person to person.
questions.misconception: Measles is caused by dirty water.

questions.stem: Describe one way measles can spread from one person to another.
answer: when an infected person coughs or sneezes near others
through droplets from the mouth or nose
hints: Think about droplets from the mouth.
Coughing and sneezing spread germs.
questions.explanation: Measles can spread through droplets from coughing and sneezing, or through close contact with an infected person.
questions.misconception: Measles cannot spread from one person to another.

questions.stem: A learner has measles. Which action will BEST help prevent other learners from getting it?
options: The sick learner should stay at home and rest
The sick learner should share books with everyone
The sick learner should play close to others
The sick learner should continue to cough in class
hints: Sick learners need rest.
Staying away reduces spread.
questions.explanation: The sick learner should stay at home and rest. This reduces the chance of spreading measles to other learners.
questions.misconception: Measles cannot spread in school.

questions.stem: What should you do if you think you have been exposed to measles?
answer: tell an adult and see a health worker
tell a parent or teacher and visit a health centre
inform an adult and go to a health worker
hints: Tell someone you trust.
A health worker can help.
questions.explanation: If you think you have been exposed to measles, tell an adult and see a health worker for advice.
questions.misconception: You should hide from health workers.

questions.stem: A learner has a fever, a rash and red eyes. A friend says, 'It is only malaria.' Why might the friend be wrong?
options: Because the learner has no cough
Because fever, rash and red eyes are common signs of measles
Because malaria does not cause fever
Because measles is caused by dirty water
hints: Measles causes fever, rash and red eyes.
These three signs together suggest measles.
questions.explanation: Fever, rash and red eyes are common signs of measles. The friend may be wrong to think it is only malaria.
questions.misconception: Measles is the same as malaria.

questions.stem: Design a simple poster to teach your class about measles. Your poster should show: (1) one cause of measles, (2) two symptoms, and (3) two ways to prevent it. Use drawings and short words.

criteria.description: Showed one correct cause of measles
Showed two correct symptoms of measles
Showed two correct ways to prevent measles
Used drawings and short words clearly

hints: Use pictures of a germ, a rash, and a vaccine.
Write short words to label your drawings.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: A rash is the only sign of measles.

questions.stem: Write a short message (3–4 sentences) for your school notice board about measles. Include what causes it, one symptom, and one way to prevent it.

criteria.description: Stated one correct cause of measles
Stated one correct symptom of measles
Stated one correct way to prevent measles
Wrote in clear sentences suitable for a school notice board

hints: Start with 'Measles is caused by...'
Mention a symptom like fever or rash.
Mention vaccination or covering the mouth.
